text:
Alex Newhook scored twice in the first period to put MTL in front, and the Canadiens never gave the lead back. Newhook, drafted 16th overall by Colorado in 2019 out of the Victoria Grizzlies, got his second on a tip-in at 13:06. Chris Kreider made it 3-0 in the second, and Jacob Fowler, a 2023 draft pick who came to the Canadiens from Boston College, held on from there.

The score hid a game TOR controlled for long stretches. Our numbers give the Leafs a 66 percent chance of winning if you replayed every shot (what we call deserved to win), and they out-attempted MTL 64 to 50. The second period was the clearest gap: TOR created 1.40 expected goals, a measure of chance quality, to MTL's 0.55, and still trailed by three. Fowler is the reason. He saved 1.6 goals more than the quality of his 28 shots against would suggest, while Sergei Bobrovsky allowed four on 28 shots and came out 1.4 goals below expectation.

TOR made it interesting in the third. William Nylander scored on the power play at 6:19, and Gavin McKenna followed 55 seconds later to cut it to 3-2. Cole Caufield had a 32 percent chance to tie it or extend the lead that Bobrovsky stopped, and Zachary Bolduc settled things with a power-play slap shot at 12:15. MTL also won the season series opener 3-2 on Sept. 29, so the Canadiens have now beaten Toronto both times they've met. The facts we have don't include either team's record or streak, so the standings picture will have to wait.
